To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel splice-site variant (c.921 +3_6del AAGT) in the RSPH4 gene was identified in nine subjects with primary ciliary dysfunction (seven families) with Hispanic ancestry, and that loss of function of the RSPH gene product was confirmed with quantitative electron microscopy analysis, measurement of the waveform and frequency of ciliary beat and transcript analysis.
we have identified a novel founder mutation in RSP4H4A that leads to a loss of protein function, resulting in a common form of PCD in patients of Puerto-Rican descent.
a founder mutation in the RSPH4 A gene was identified in patients with primary ciliary dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a founder mutation in RSP4H4A in Hispanic patients with primary ciliary dykinesia (H-PCD).
the genetic basis of PCD, which has been difficult to identify in patients without situs abnormalities.
the identification of a founder mutation in RSPSH4A in patients of Hispanic ancestry, and the importance of genetic testing to improve diagnosis and management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a novel splice-site founder mutation in RSP4A, identified in patients of Puerto Rico descent with PCD.
the c.921+6delAAGTT mutation in the RSPH4a gene is a founder mutation in PCD patients of Hispanic descent.
the c.921+5_6delAATG mutation in RSPSH4A is the most common cause of PDC in Puerto Rico.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified a novel RSPH4 mutation that is a founder mutation in Puerto Rican PCD patients and we also identified the mechanism of disease for this mutation.
we have identified a novel splice-site founder mutation in the RSPH4 gene that is associated with a common phenotype in patients of Puerto Rico descent.
the identification of the c.921+6_3delAAGT mutation in RSP4A is important for the diagnosis of PCD in patients with Hispanic ancestry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the c.921+ 3_6del AAGT mutation in RSPSH4A is the cause of PCD in Hispanic patients of Puerto Rican ancestry.
genetic testing is crucial to confirm the diagnosis of PCD and to provide accurate genetic counseling.
genetic testing should be considered in patients with PCD, particularly in patients of Hispanic ancestry, and should include testing of RSPH4a.
